discussion:
Requiring human user involvement in the protective marking of emails ensures a conscious decision is made. This lessens the chance of incorrect protective markings being automatically applied to emails. In addition, only allowing the selection of protective markings for which a system is authorised to process, store or communicate lessens the chance of inadvertently over-classifying emails.

Email content filters may only check the most recent protective marking applied to emails. Therefore, when responding to or forwarding emails, requiring protective markings that are at least as high as that of emails that are received will help email content filters prevent emails being sent to systems that are not authorised to handle their original sensitivity or classification.
title: When replying to or forwarding emails, protective marking tools do not allow the selection of protective markings lower than previously used.
